Senses.Explanation: To gain life within death: the phrase functions as a public-interview question, an appraisal, and one side of an explicit death-and-life contrast. It is asked directly in public interview — ‘what about when one gains life within death?’ — and receives different recorded answers, including ‘night travel is not permitted; you must arrive at daylight.’ In the Piyun–Magu encounter, Piyun declares ‘gain life within death—one in ten thousand,’ after first acting as though Magu were dead; other masters apply the phrase as an appraisal after the recorded questioner claps, or place it beside ‘revive after being cut off.’ A verse draws the corpus's own contrast: ‘people who gain life within death are numberless; those who gain death within life have been rare from ancient times.’ These are attested questions, appraisals, sequences, and contrasts; the entry does not decide what death or life denotes beyond the recorded phrase.
